definition: Static Site Generator. A tool that pre-renders web pages at build time into static HTML files.
Server-Side Rendering. A technique where HTML is generated on the server per request rather than in the browser.
The process of attaching JavaScript event listeners and state to static HTML already rendered on the server or at build time.
Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery. The practice of automating build, test, and deployment pipelines on every code change.
An automated sequence of steps (build, test, deploy) triggered by a code event such as a push or pull request.
An approach to writing documentation using the same tools and workflows as software development: version control, pull requests, and automated publishing.
Darwin Information Typing Architecture. An XML standard for structuring technical documentation into reusable topic types: task, concept, and reference.
Representational State Transfer. An architectural style for APIs that uses HTTP methods and stateless, resource-based URLs.
A specification format for describing REST APIs in a machine-readable YAML or JSON document, enabling documentation generation and contract testing.
The elimination of dead (unreachable) code from a JavaScript bundle at build time, reducing final bundle size.
